title: Fixed Four Transverse Rollers and Open Sided Bearing Shoe
description: One wholly newly authored complete dry roller-bearing-inspired architectural support unit. Four whole full-width transverse barrel-ended steel-coloured rollers sit between one full flat lower track and a separate broad upper bearing shoe. Each roller has a complete through-axle exterior with two integral broad shoulder collars, and two whole narrow cage cheeks contain four bounded square axle apertures apiece. The collars overlap the outer cheek margins in the fixed display while their inner faces are offset from the cheek surfaces; the long open intervals above and below the cheeks leave the roller bodies visible. One whole grounded plate and the separate upper shoe each contain four real bounded mounting apertures. Unlike the recovered spherical support, there is no circular concave dish, single convex sliding shoe or narrow central neck; this is a linear pack of independent full cylinders between wide parallel seats. Unlike an annular ball-bearing display, there are no concentric inner/outer races or circumferential row of balls. All numeric plates, cylinders, shoulder axles and cage boundaries independently authored together; no earlier bearing, conveyor, fairlead, plate or roller mesh imported or extracted. Four opaque constant untextured PBR roles, metres native Z up and complete horizontal bounds-centred ground sole, one architectural model zero scenes. Generic fixed support artwork only, not an engineered expansion bearing or a manufacturer model. Small deliberate fixed contact overlaps establish visual roots, not a solved fit, lubricant layer or operating mechanism. No rolling travel, rotation, articulation, thermal expansion accommodation, load transfer, pressure, friction, seismic isolation, fastening, fatigue, fabrication, installation or structural safety capability made or verified. No host structure, rigging, animation or interaction.
